scope: Bold the Lens Data column-header row identified in the user's screenshot, preserving existing worktree changes.
implementation: Use a Lens Data grid-local style setting the native DataGridColumnHeader font weight to Bold (700). Numeric TextBlock header content inherits this weight.
Keep existing font sizes, column widths, numeric right alignment, colors and data-row font weights. Unrelated DataGrid headers retain their original typography.
Document the presentation change in the maintained user guide. No optical algorithm or reference data changed.

renderingCases.assertions: Compare header font size with an unmodified same-theme DataGrid, check actual header TextBlocks are bold, numeric alignment is right, data rows and input boxes remain normal, unrelated headers are not bold, and workspace revision is unchanged.

preservedIntermediateEvidence: header-initial.log: the new test required the Avalonia.Layout import for HorizontalAlignment; the harness was corrected.

header-typography.trx: ten typography cases failed an incorrect assumption that native header font size followed the editor's 13/18 setting; two layout tests passed. The native theme header size was 12. The corrected assertion compares against an unmodified native header in the same theme rather than altering production font sizes.
header-baseline-checked.trx: the corrected ten typography cases plus two layout cases passed before the final broader regression runs.

representativeCapture.meaning: Real Lens Data controls rendered offscreen with bold headers and normal data, plus an unrelated normal-weight comparison table below. Visually inspected without capturing the user's screen.

countingRule: Scoped regression and isolated rendering collections overlap and must not be added. Default application compilation occurred through the targeted test project build, not a fresh full root-solution build.
